# Linear Models

Welcome to the Linear Models knowledge base.

This document is designed to serve two purposes:

1. **Course reference:** everything explicitly taught in the Linear Models course.
2. **Mathematical reference:** prerequisite material needed to understand the course, even when that material is taught elsewhere or is not part of the syllabus.

The goal is not simply to reproduce lecture notes, but to map the mathematical structure connecting the topics.

---

## How to use this document

The material is divided into three main sections:

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="33%"}

### Core

Material explicitly taught in the Linear Models course.

These topics are the primary focus for coursework and examinations.

:::

::: {.column width="33%"}

### Prerequisites

Mathematical and statistical concepts needed to understand the Core material.

Some of these may be taught in other courses and may not be directly examinable in Linear Models.

:::

## Understanding the status of a topic

Each topic can have two different kinds of importance.

### Course relevance

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 🟢 **Core** | Explicitly taught and examinable |
| 🟡 **Supporting** | Not necessarily examinable, but needed to understand Core material |
| ⚪ **Background** | Useful background knowledge |
| 🔵 **Extension** | Beyond the requirements of the course |

### Required depth

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **1 · Recognize** | Understand the idea and terminology |
| **2 · Apply** | Perform calculations or use the result |
| **3 · Derive** | Derive important results |
| **4 · Prove** | Understand or reproduce proofs |

A prerequisite therefore does **not** automatically mean "study the entire subject."

For example, Linear Models may require a working understanding of orthogonal projections without requiring the full theory of abstract inner-product spaces.

---

## The dependency structure

The important question is not only:

> "What comes next in the lectures?"

but also:

> "What does this topic depend on?"

A simplified dependency structure might look like:

```text
Linear Algebra
      │
      ├── Vectors
      ├── Matrices
      ├── Subspaces
      ├── Orthogonality
      │
      └──────────────┐
                     ↓
                Projections
                     │
                     ↓
                Least Squares
                     │
                     ↓
                Linear Model
                     │
              ┌──────┴──────┐
              ↓             ↓
         Estimation      Residuals
              │             │
              └──────┬──────┘
                     ↓
                 Inference
```
